rich_summary: When the fiery sage Durvasa arrives during a secret audience between Rama and the personified Death, Lakshmana must choose between obeying Rama’s command not to interrupt and preventing the sage from unleashing a catastrophic curse on the kingdom. Deciding that his own life is worth less than the destruction of all others, Lakshmana interrupts and announces the sage. Rama receives Durvasa and feeds him after his thousand‑year fast, but the vow tied to the interrupted meeting forces a terrible consequence. Guided by the counsel of the priest Vasishtha, Rama declares Lakshmana banished—equivalent to death for a man of honor. Accepting fate calmly, Lakshmana goes to the Sarayu, enters deep meditation, and is taken bodily to heaven, revealed as a divine portion of Vishnu.

highlight_spans.why: Durvasa’s furious threat to curse the entire kingdom creates the crisis that forces Lakshmana’s tragic choice.
Lakshmana’s resolve that he alone should perish rather than let others be destroyed defines his heroic self‑sacrifice.
Vasishtha explains the cosmic stakes: a broken vow could endanger the Three Worlds, framing the decision as a matter of universal dharma.
Rama’s heartbreaking declaration of banishment shows the conflict between personal love and uncompromising righteousness.
Lakshmana’s final meditation by the Sarayu and ascent with divine honors reveals his true divine nature.

top_scenes.scene_text: Lakshmana stands at the palace entrance while the blazing sage Durvasa threatens to curse the kingdom, forcing the prince to choose between duty and catastrophe.
Rama, grief-stricken before the royal assembly, declares Lakshmana’s banishment while the loyal brother stands weeping yet resolute.
On the banks of the Sarayu, Lakshmana meditates motionless as gods, apsaras, and rishis shower flowers while Indra bears him invisibly toward heaven.
